record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Under a believable cryptographic assumption, can one show that catalytic logspace CL is contained in some plausible subclass of P, perhaps even NC?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Show CL is contained in some subclass of P, perhaps NC, given a believable cryptographic assumption.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Define catalytic logspace, denoted CL, as the class of decision problems decidable by a deterministic Turing machine that has (i) a read-only input tape of length n, (ii) a read/write work tape of length O(log n), and (iii) a read/write auxiliary "catalytic" tape of length 2^{O(log n)} = poly(n) which is initialized to an arbitrary string and is required to be restored to its exact initial contents at the end of every computation, regardless of the input. The machine must accept or reject correctly for every input on every possible initial contents of the catalytic tape.

Let P denote deterministic polynomial time, and let NC denote the class of problems solvable by uniform Boolean circuits of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth (with fan-in 2 gates). It is known that L ⊆ CL ⊆ ZPP, and CL contains uniform TC^1, but no nontrivial upper bound of CL inside P is known.

Problem. Assuming some believable cryptographic hardness assumption (for example, the existence of one-way functions, hardness of factoring, or hardness of discrete logarithm), prove that CL ⊆ C for some plausible proper subclass C of P. In particular, determine whether one can establish CL ⊆ NC under such a cryptographic assumption.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of placing CL in any proper subclass of P (such as NC) remains open. Recent work (2025) showing bipartite matching and linear matroid intersection lie in CL is interpreted as a barrier to placing CL in the NC hierarchy and suggests CL may be more powerful than previously believed. No cryptographic-assumption-based upper bound on CL inside NC appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Bipartite Matching is in Catalytic Logspace
status_evidence.snippet: shows bipartite matching in CL, viewed as a barrier to CL ⊆ NC
status_evidence.claim: Recent results suggest CL may not be contained in NC, leaving the upper-bound question open.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of In-Place Space-Bounded Computation
status_evidence.snippet: surveys catalytic computation and open problems on upper bounds for CL
status_evidence.claim: No known unconditional or cryptographic upper bound placing CL in a proper subclass of P.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic Logspace: Complexity & Applications
status_evidence.snippet: CL ⊆ ZPP is the best known general upper bound; containment in NC remains open
status_evidence.claim: Containment of CL in NC remains an open problem.
